Title: 15th of June: Morning discussion with Fernando Meirelles
Chunks: 0,1
On the Saturday morning discussion, Brazilian director **Fernando Meirelles** told about his versatile career, which has included various works from video art to successful international films and from experimental TV series to opera.
Meirelles remembers his first film experiences are related to his father’s movie clips which were shot on 16mm film. However, the career as a director was not Meirelles’s original plan. He grew up in São Paulo and after discontinuing his biology studies Meirelles studied architecture. He decided to become a filmmaker after seeing **Jorge Bodanzky** and **Orlando Senna**’s _Iracema_ (1975). It was a film that combined fiction and documentary such an exceptional way and was so impressive for Meirelles that he decided to make a short film as his final project and, as a result, made his introduction to the film industry.
At the beginning of his career, Meirelles and his colleagues made experimental short films and video art. He also directed several years fun and experimental series and worked in advertising. However, the ads were not enough for Meirelles – instead, he dreamed of directing a feature film. He practiced directing a feature film with his first film _Maids_ (2001).
“I always want to get involved in projects that make me feel insecure. The topics I don’t know much about and I usually even regret, that I agreed to take on such an impossible idea. For some reason, these work the best in the end.”
Meirelles wanted to film **José Saramago**‘s novel _Blindness_, but because of the copyrights, the plan was almost canceled. One of the luckiest coincidences on Meirelles’s career was when the publisher of Saramago asked if Meirelles would be interested in directing **Paulo Lins**‘s novel _The City of God_. After a short moment of hesitation, Meirelles grasped this opportunity and chose a completely different topic.

Meirelles’s The City of God was screened at the Cannes Film Festival and was a great success. The film was followed by another success, _The Constant Gardener_ (2005), after which Meirelles announced that he would stop making movies. However, he went back on his decision, as he finally got the opportunity to direct a film adaption of Blindness (2008). The film was followed by _360_ (2011) and then Meirelles returned to TV series. Even after that the director has still broken new ground.
Trying something new has always inspired Meirelles. He has directed, for example, the opera _Les Pêcheurs de Perles_ in 2015 and the opening ceremony of the Olympic Games in Rio de Janeiro in 2016. Currently, the director has many projects in progress, including a climate crisis series for the BBC, a science documentary and the feature film _The Pope_ produced by Netflix.
Meirelles would bring the film Iracema with him to a deserted island. That movie which originally encouraged him to become a director.

_**The Constant Gardener**_ is a 2005 [drama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drama_(film_and_television) "Drama (film and television)")[thriller](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thriller_(genre) "Thriller (genre)") film[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Constant_Gardener_(film)#cite_note-3) directed by [Fernando Meirelles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fernando_Meirelles "Fernando Meirelles"). The screenplay by [Jeffrey Caine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeffrey_Caine "Jeffrey Caine") is based on [John le Carré](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_le_Carr%C3%A9 "John le Carré")'s [2001 novel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Constant_Gardener "The Constant Gardener"). The story follows Justin Quayle ([Ralph Fiennes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ralph_Fiennes "Ralph Fiennes")), a British diplomat in Kenya, as he tries to solve the murder of his wife Tessa ([Rachel Weisz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rachel_Weisz "Rachel Weisz")), an [Amnesty International](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amnesty_International "Amnesty International") activist, alternating with [flashbacks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flashback_(narrative) "Flashback (narrative)") telling the story of their relationship.
The film's title derives from Justin's gentle but diligent attention to his plants throughout the film. The film was a critical and box office success and earned four [Oscar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Awards "Academy Awards") nominations, winning [Best Supporting Actress](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Award_for_Best_Supporting_Actress "Academy Award for Best Supporting Actress") for Weisz.

British diplomat and avid horticulturalist Justin Quayle is confronted by [Amnesty International](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amnesty_International "Amnesty International") activist Tessa during a lecture in London. They strike up a romance, and marry after she accompanies him to his posting in [Kenya](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya "Kenya"). She befriends Belgian doctor Arnold Bluhm, leading to rumours of an affair. Tessa has no qualms confronting corruption, to the chagrin of Justin's superiors, and she loses a child late in pregnancy.
Tessa and Arnold connect recent local deaths to [drug trials](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clinical_trial "Clinical trial") being conducted by the Kenyan-based company Three Bees using the drug Dypraxa. They write a damaging report on the drug and Tessa gives it to Justin's colleague Sandy Woodrow, the British [High Commissioner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/High_Commissioner "High Commissioner"), who sends it to Sir Bernard Pellegrin, head of the Africa Desk at the [Foreign Office](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Foreign,_Commonwealth_and_Development_Office "Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office"). Pellegrin responds with an incriminating letter to Sandy, which Tessa persuades him to show her, and she steals it before departing for [Lokichogio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lokichogio "Lokichogio") with Arnold.
Sandy informs Justin that a white woman and black driver have been killed near [Lake Turkana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lake_Turkana "Lake Turkana"), and that Tessa and Arnold shared a room at [Lodwar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lodwar "Lodwar") before hiring a car. Justin and Sandy identify Tessa's mutilated body, but Arnold's whereabouts remain unknown. Police confiscate Tessa's computer and files, but Justin finds her keepsake box, containing a letter from Sandy declaring his love for her and asking her to return Pellegrin's letter, and records of Three Bees' tests.

After Tessa's burial, Justin learns from his colleague Ghita that Tessa kept Arnold's secret that he was gay, as [homosexuality is illegal in Kenya](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/LGBT_rights_in_Kenya "LGBT rights in Kenya"). Pursuing the truth about his wife's murder, he follows the trail of her report. Justin is briefly detained by police and confronts Three Bees' CEO Kenny Curtiss, but receives no answers.
Returning to London, Justin's passport is confiscated. He dines with Pellegrin, who lies that Arnold must have murdered Tessa, and believes that Justin has his incriminating letter. Justin meets with Tessa's cousin and lawyer Ham, and they access her computer files to reveal her investigation into Dypraxa and its manufacturer, [Swiss](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Switzerland "Switzerland")-[Canadian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canada "Canada")[pharmaceutical conglomerate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pharmaceutical_industry "Pharmaceutical industry") KDH, which hired Three Bees to test the drug on unsuspecting Kenyans as a treatment for [tuberculosis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tuberculosis "Tuberculosis").
Justin receives a threatening note and Ham provides him with a fake passport to travel to Germany to meet with Tessa's contact Birgit. She is part of a pharmaceutical watchdog group and is reluctant to speak due to the targeting of her group. Justin is attacked in his hotel room and warned to stop investigating. Arnold's body is found having been tortured to death, while the announcement of a safe Dypraxa causes KDH's share price to soar.
Returning to Kenya, Justin confronts Sandy, who admits that Tessa's report was silenced to save KDH from spending millions redeveloping the drug. Justin is approached by Curtiss, who has been betrayed by KDH, and brought to a mass grave of Dypraxa test subjects. Curtiss points Justin to Dr Lorbeer, Dypraxa's inventor, who has fled to [Sudan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sudan "Sudan"). Tim Donohue, a friend in British intelligence, confirms that Pellegrin had Tessa and Arnold killed. Unable to convince Justin to return home, he gives him a gun.

Justin travels to confront Lorbeer, who is treating remote villagers to atone for the lives claimed by his drug. The village is attacked by raiders, but Justin and Lorbeer escape in a [UN](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations "United Nations") aid plane, and Lorbeer reveals that he has Pellegrin's letter. Tessa convinced him to record the truth about Dypraxa, but he changed his mind, instead informing KDH that Tessa and Arnold were en route to expose the company to the UN.
Justin convinces the pilot to mail Pellegrin's letter to Ham, and to drop him off at Lake Turkana. Removing the bullets from his gun, his final thoughts are of Tessa before he is killed by KDH's henchmen. In London at Tessa and Justin's memorial service, Pellegrin lies that Justin committed suicide in the same place his wife died.
Ham announces the reading of an [epistle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Epistle "Epistle"), but instead reads Pellegrin's letter, exposing the deaths caused by Dypraxa and the subsequent coverup. Pellegrin storms out as Ham implicates the British government, KDH, and public complacency regarding the human cost of medicine they take for granted.

## Inspiration and themes
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=The_Constant_Gardener_(film)&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Inspiration and themes")]
The plot of the film is loosely based on a [real-life case in Kano, Nigeria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abdullahi_v._Pfizer,_Inc. "Abdullahi v. Pfizer, Inc.") involving antibacterial testing by Pfizer on small children.
The film was shot partly in [16mm](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/16mm "16mm")[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Constant_Gardener_(film)#cite_note-4) on location in [Loiyangalani](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Loiyangalani "Loiyangalani") and the slums of [Kibera](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kibera "Kibera"), a section of [Nairobi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nairobi "Nairobi"), [Kenya](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya "Kenya"). Circumstances in the area so affected the cast and crew that producer [Simon Channing Williams](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Simon_Channing_Williams "Simon Channing Williams") led the creation of the Constant Gardener Trust in order to address issues of sanitation and education in the area.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Constant_Gardener_(film)#cite_note-5)[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Constant_Gardener_(film)#cite_note-6)[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Constant_Gardener_(film)#cite_note-7)
Principal photography of the film occurred from May 10, 2004 to August 7, 2004.
[Kate Winslet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kate_Winslet "Kate Winslet") and [Eva Green](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eva_Green "Eva Green") were considered for the female lead before Weisz was cast.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Constant_Gardener_(film)#cite_note-8)

## Inspiration and themes
[Lupita Nyong'o](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lupita_Nyong'o "Lupita Nyong'o") worked as a production assistant on the film.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Constant_Gardener_(film)#cite_note-9)
The film's worldwide gross was $82,466,670.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Constant_Gardener_(film)#cite_note-10)
On the film aggregator website [Rotten Tomatoes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rotten_Tomatoes "Rotten Tomatoes"), _The Constant Gardener_ has a score of 83%, based on 192 critical reviews, with an average rating of 7.6/10. The consensus reads, "_The Constant Gardener_ is a smart, gripping, and suspenseful thriller with rich performances from the leads."[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Constant_Gardener_(film)#cite_note-the_constant_gardener-2) It also has a score of 82 out of 100 on [Metacritic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metacritic "Metacritic"), based on 39 critics.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Constant_Gardener_(film)#cite_note-11) Audiences polled by [CinemaScore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CinemaScore "CinemaScore") gave the film an average grade of "B" on an A+ to F scale.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Constant_Gardener_(film)#cite_note-12)

Sandy informs Justin that a white woman and black driver have been killed near [Lake Turkana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lake_Turkana "Lake Turkana"), and that Tessa and Arnold shared a room at [Lodwar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lodwar "Lodwar") before hiring a car. Justin and Sandy identify Tessa's mutilated body, but Arnold's whereabouts remain unknown. Police confiscate Tessa's computer and files, but Justin finds her keepsake box, containing a letter from Sandy declaring his love for her and asking her to return Pellegrin's letter, and records of Three Bees' tests.
texts.4:
After Tessa's burial, Justin learns from his colleague Ghita that Tessa kept Arnold's secret that he was gay, as [homosexuality is illegal in Kenya](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/LGBT_rights_in_Kenya "LGBT rights in Kenya"). Pursuing the truth about his wife's murder, he follows the trail of her report. Justin is briefly detained by police and confronts Three Bees' CEO Kenny Curtiss, but receives no answers.
Returning to London, Justin's passport is confiscated. He dines with Pellegrin, who lies that Arnold must have murdered Tessa, and believes that Justin has his incriminating letter. Justin meets with Tessa's cousin and lawyer Ham, and they access her computer files to reveal her investigation into Dypraxa and its manufacturer, [Swiss](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Switzerland "Switzerland")-[Canadian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canada "Canada")[pharmaceutical conglomerate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pharmaceutical_industry "Pharmaceutical industry") KDH, which hired Three Bees to test the drug on unsuspecting Kenyans as a treatment for [tuberculosis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tuberculosis "Tuberculosis").
Justin receives a threatening note and Ham provides him with a fake passport to travel to Germany to meet with Tessa's contact Birgit. She is part of a pharmaceutical watchdog group and is reluctant to speak due to the targeting of her group. Justin is attacked in his hotel room and warned to stop investigating. Arnold's body is found having been tortured to death, while the announcement of a safe Dypraxa causes KDH's share price to soar.
Returning to Kenya, Justin confronts Sandy, who admits that Tessa's report was silenced to save KDH from spending millions redeveloping the drug. Justin is approached by Curtiss, who has been betrayed by KDH, and brought to a mass grave of Dypraxa test subjects. Curtiss points Justin to Dr Lorbeer, Dypraxa's inventor, who has fled to [Sudan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sudan "Sudan"). Tim Donohue, a friend in British intelligence, confirms that Pellegrin had Tessa and Arnold killed. Unable to convince Justin to return home, he gives him a gun.
texts.5:
Justin travels to confront Lorbeer, who is treating remote villagers to atone for the lives claimed by his drug. The village is attacked by raiders, but Justin and Lorbeer escape in a [UN](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations "United Nations") aid plane, and Lorbeer reveals that he has Pellegrin's letter. Tessa convinced him to record the truth about Dypraxa, but he changed his mind, instead informing KDH that Tessa and Arnold were en route to expose the company to the UN.
Justin convinces the pilot to mail Pellegrin's letter to Ham, and to drop him off at Lake Turkana. Removing the bullets from his gun, his final thoughts are of Tessa before he is killed by KDH's henchmen. In London at Tessa and Justin's memorial service, Pellegrin lies that Justin committed suicide in the same place his wife died.
Ham announces the reading of an [epistle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Epistle "Epistle"), but instead reads Pellegrin's letter, exposing the deaths caused by Dypraxa and the subsequent coverup. Pellegrin storms out as Ham implicates the British government, KDH, and public complacency regarding the human cost of medicine they take for granted.

## Inspiration and themes
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=The_Constant_Gardener_(film)&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Inspiration and themes")]
The plot of the film is loosely based on a [real-life case in Kano, Nigeria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abdullahi_v._Pfizer,_Inc. "Abdullahi v. Pfizer, Inc.") involving antibacterial testing by Pfizer on small children.
The film was shot partly in [16mm](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/16mm "16mm")[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Constant_Gardener_(film)#cite_note-4) on location in [Loiyangalani](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Loiyangalani "Loiyangalani") and the slums of [Kibera](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kibera "Kibera"), a section of [Nairobi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nairobi "Nairobi"), [Kenya](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya "Kenya"). Circumstances in the area so affected the cast and crew that producer [Simon Channing Williams](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Simon_Channing_Williams "Simon Channing Williams") led the creation of the Constant Gardener Trust in order to address issues of sanitation and education in the area.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Constant_Gardener_(film)#cite_note-5)[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Constant_Gardener_(film)#cite_note-6)[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Constant_Gardener_(film)#cite_note-7)
Principal photography of the film occurred from May 10, 2004 to August 7, 2004.
[Kate Winslet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kate_Winslet "Kate Winslet") and [Eva Green](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eva_Green "Eva Green") were considered for the female lead before Weisz was cast.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Constant_Gardener_(film)#cite_note-8)

**Peter King Nzioki Mwania** (born 25 May 1978), popularly known as **Peter King**, is a Kenyan actor.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Nzioki#cite_note-1)[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Nzioki#cite_note-pulse-2) He is best known for his roles in the films _[The Constant Gardener](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Constant\_Gardener\_(film) "The Constant Gardener (film)")_, _[The Fifth Estate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Fifth\_Estate\_(film) "The Fifth Estate (film)")_ and _[Sense8](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sense8 "Sense8")_.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Nzioki#cite_note-pulse-2)
Nzioki was born on 25 May 1978 in [Nairobi, Kenya](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nairobi "Nairobi"). His father Michael David Mwania, served in the [Kenyan Army](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya_Army "Kenya Army") and his mother worked at the military hospital. At the age of six, he joined church productions at the [Lang’ata](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lang'ata "Lang'ata") Barracks. He completed his education from Lang’ata High School in [Nairobi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nairobi "Nairobi").[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Nzioki#cite_note-kenyabuzz-3)
He is married to fellow actress Tess King.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Nzioki#cite_note-4)

He made his acting debut in 2000 at the [Kenya](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya "Kenya") National Theatre for three years under the guidance of Joab Kanuka. In theater, he played 'Iago' in the Phoenix Players production of the [Shakespeare](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Shakespeare "William Shakespeare") tragedy _[Othello](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Othello "Othello")_. In 2005, he made his film debut with a minor role in _[The Constant Gardener](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Constant\_Gardener\_(film) "The Constant Gardener (film)")_ directed by [Fernando Meirelles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fernando_Meirelles "Fernando Meirelles").[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Nzioki#cite_note-kenyabuzz-3) In the same year, he appeared as 'Barman' in the television movie _[Transit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transit\_(2005\_film) "Transit (2005 film)")_. In 2016, he appeared in the thriller film _[The CEO](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_CEO "The CEO")_ where he played the role of 'Jomo'. The film had its premier 10 July 2016, at the Eko Hotels & Suites, [Victoria Island, Lagos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Victoria_Island,_Lagos "Victoria Island, Lagos")[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Nzioki#cite_note-5) and later received critical acclaim.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Nzioki#cite_note-pulse-2)[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Nzioki#cite_note-6)[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Nzioki#cite_note-7)

He made some notable appearances as 'Mkwajo' in award-winning musical _Mo Faya_ directed by [Eric Wainaina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eric_Wainaina_(musician) "Eric Wainaina (musician)"); scheming spouse in _[Facebook](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Facebook "Facebook")_ and corrupt politician 'Mzito' in _Ni Sisi_. After several villainous roles, he received the role as stepfather in [MTV](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MTV "MTV") series [_Shuga 2_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shuga_(TV_series) "Shuga (TV series)"), then as an inspiring soccer coach in _The Inside Story_ aired in Discovery Channel; and a preacher in _The Knife Grinder's Tale_.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Nzioki#cite_note-8)
In 2016, he was selected for the role as Kenyan crime lord '[Silas Kabaka](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sense8 "Sense8")' in the [Netflix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netflix "Netflix") series _[Sense8](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sense8 "Sense8")_.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Nzioki#cite_note-pulse-2) The role made him a popular television actor in [Kenya](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya "Kenya").

**Rachel Hannah Weisz** (;[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rachel_Weisz#cite_note-2) born 7 March 1970)[[note 1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rachel_Weisz#cite_note-birthplace-9) is a British actress. Known for her performances on stage and screen, she has received [several awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_awards_and_nominations_received_by_Rachel_Weisz "List of awards and nominations received by Rachel Weisz"), including an [Academy Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Award "Academy Award"), an [Actor Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Actor_Award "Actor Award"), a [BAFTA Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BAFTA_Award "BAFTA Award"), a [Golden Globe Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Award "Golden Globe Award"), and a [Laurence Olivier Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laurence_Olivier_Award "Laurence Olivier Award").
Weisz began acting in stage and television productions in the early 1990s, and made her film debut in _[Death Machine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Death\_Machine "Death Machine")_ (1994). She won a [Critics' Circle Theatre Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Critics'_Circle_Theatre_Award "Critics' Circle Theatre Award") for her role in the 1994 revival of [Noël Coward](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/No%C3%ABl_Coward "Noël Coward")'s play _[Design for Living](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Design\_for\_Living "Design for Living")_, and went on to appear in the 1999 [Donmar Warehouse](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Donmar_Warehouse "Donmar Warehouse") production of [Tennessee Williams](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tennessee_Williams "Tennessee Williams")' drama _[Suddenly Last Summer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Suddenly\_Last\_Summer "Suddenly Last Summer")_.

Her film breakthrough came with her starring role as [Evelyn Carnahan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Evelyn_Carnahan "Evelyn Carnahan") in the Hollywood action films _[The Mummy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Mummy\_(1999\_film) "The Mummy (1999 film)")_ (1999) and _[The Mummy Returns](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Mummy\_Returns "The Mummy Returns")_ (2001).[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rachel_Weisz#cite_note-hollywood_debut-10) Weisz went on to star in several films of the 2000s, including _[Enemy at the Gates](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Enemy\_at\_the\_Gates "Enemy at the Gates")_ (2001), _[About a Boy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/About\_a\_Boy\_(film) "About a Boy (film)")_ (2002), _[Runaway Jury](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Runaway\_Jury "Runaway Jury")_ (2003), _[Constantine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Constantine\_(film) "Constantine (film)")_ (2005), _[The Fountain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Fountain "The Fountain")_ (2006), _[Definitely, Maybe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Definitely,\_Maybe "Definitely, Maybe")_ (2008), _[The Lovely Bones](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Lovely\_Bones\_(film) "The Lovely Bones (film)")_ (2009) and _[The Whistleblower](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Whistleblower "The Whistleblower")_ (2010).

For her performance as an activist in the 2005 thriller _[The Constant Gardener](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Constant\_Gardener\_(film) "The Constant Gardener (film)")_, she won the [Academy Award for Best Supporting Actress](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Award_for_Best_Supporting_Actress "Academy Award for Best Supporting Actress"), and for playing [Blanche DuBois](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blanche_DuBois "Blanche DuBois") in a 2009 revival of _[A Streetcar Named Desire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A\_Streetcar\_Named\_Desire "A Streetcar Named Desire")_, she won the [Laurence Olivier Award for Best Actress](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laurence_Olivier_Award_for_Best_Actress "Laurence Olivier Award for Best Actress"). In the 2010s, Weisz continued to star in big-budget films such as the action film _[The Bourne Legacy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Bourne\_Legacy\_(film) "The Bourne Legacy (film)")_ (2012) and the fantasy film _[Oz the Great and Powerful](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oz\_the\_Great\_and\_Powerful "Oz the Great and Powerful")_ (2013) and achieved critical acclaim for her performances in the independent films _[The Deep Blue Sea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Deep\_Blue\_Sea\_(2011\_film) "The Deep Blue Sea (2011 film)")_ (2011), _[Denial](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Denial\_(2016\_film) "Denial (2016 film)")_ (2016), and _[The Favourite](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Favourite\_(2018\_film) "The Favourite (2018 film)")_ (2018).

For her portrayal of [Sarah Churchill](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sarah_Churchill,_Duchess_of_Marlborough "Sarah Churchill, Duchess of Marlborough") in _The Favourite_, she won the [BAFTA Award for Best Actress in a Supporting Role](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BAFTA_Award_for_Best_Actress_in_a_Supporting_Role "BAFTA Award for Best Actress in a Supporting Role") and received a second Academy Award nomination.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rachel_Weisz#cite_note-11) Weisz portrayed [Melina Vostokoff](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Melina_Vostokoff_(Marvel_Cinematic_Universe) "Melina Vostokoff (Marvel Cinematic Universe)") in the [Marvel Cinematic Universe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marvel_Cinematic_Universe "Marvel Cinematic Universe") film _[Black Widow](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black\_Widow\_(2021\_film) "Black Widow (2021 film)")_ (2021) and starred as twin obstetricians in the thriller miniseries _[Dead Ringers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dead\_Ringers\_(miniseries) "Dead Ringers (miniseries)")_ (2023).

Austria.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rachel_Weisz#cite_note-thisislondon-21)[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rachel_Weisz#cite_note-22) Her maternal grandfather's ancestry was [Austrian Jewish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Austrian_Jewish "Austrian Jewish");

**Peter King Nzioki Mwania** (born 25 May 1978), popularly known as **Peter King**, is a Kenyan actor.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Nzioki#cite_note-1)[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Nzioki#cite_note-pulse-2) He is best known for his roles in the films _[The Constant Gardener](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Constant\_Gardener\_(film) "The Constant Gardener (film)")_, _[The Fifth Estate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Fifth\_Estate\_(film) "The Fifth Estate (film)")_ and _[Sense8](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sense8 "Sense8")_.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Nzioki#cite_note-pulse-2)
Nzioki was born on 25 May 1978 in [Nairobi, Kenya](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nairobi "Nairobi"). His father Michael David Mwania, served in the [Kenyan Army](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya_Army "Kenya Army") and his mother worked at the military hospital. At the age of six, he joined church productions at the [Lang’ata](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lang'ata "Lang'ata") Barracks. He completed his education from Lang’ata High School in [Nairobi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nairobi "Nairobi").[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Nzioki#cite_note-kenyabuzz-3)
He is married to fellow actress Tess King.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Nzioki#cite_note-4)
texts.1: He made his acting debut in 2000 at the [Kenya](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya "Kenya") National Theatre for three years under the guidance of Joab Kanuka. In 2016, he appeared in the thriller film _[The CEO](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_CEO "The CEO")_ where he played the role of 'Jomo'. Galloping forward into the seventh place of the Chinese zodiac is the free-spirited and elegant Horse. Unfortunately, during the Jade Emperor’s great race to determine the animals of the zodiac, the Horse was cheated! As it headed towards the finish line, the Snake emerged from where it had been hiding under its hoof and terrified it, causing it to lurch back and allowing the Snake to slither into sixth place. For this reason, horses will always stomp on snakes when they see them!
**_Years of the Horse_**
![Image 1](https://www.asiaculturaltravel.co.uk/wp-content/uploads/2020/01/hourse.jpeg)
If you were born in the year 1930, 1942, 1954, 1966, 1978, 1990, 2002, 2014, or 2026 then you belong to the sign of the Horse. It’s important to note that the Chinese zodiac follows the Chinese lunar calendar, which begins in late-January or early-February. For example, Chinese New Year fell on January 21 st in 1966, so anyone born before that date actually belongs to the Year of the Snake and not the Year of the Horse. In short, you’ve just become your own worst enemy!
**_Lucky Signs and Symbols_**
Those born in the Year of the Horse should take note of the numbers 1, 2, 3, 5, 6, and 7. Two, three, and seven are sure to bring you good fortune, but one, five, and six are to be avoided at all costs! Green and yellow are your lucky colours, while disaster comes in the form of blue and white.
**_Characteristics of the Horse_**
With their boundless energy and thirst for adventure, Horse people are said to be lively, humorous, sociable, warm-hearted, easy-going, generous, and fiercely independent. Their optimistic attitude and witty repartee means they attract friends with ease, and their strength of character allows them to effortlessly overcome difficulties. Whether it’s at concerts, performances, meetings, sporting events, or parties, Horses love to be part of the crowd.

Unfortunately, the Horse’s positive attributes are the direct source of their weaknesses. With all the social activities they engage in, Horse people are prone to spending far too much money and can quickly find themselves in debt if they don’t manage their finances carefully. Their openness means that they are terrible at keeping secrets, and their superficial wit belies a general dearth of concrete knowledge. While they may come across as self-centred, their lack of academic intelligence means their self-confidence can actually be quite low.
**_Romantic Compatibility_**
Romantically speaking, the Horse should look to the Tiger or the Sheep for a lasting relationship, although they can forge a pleasant relationship with the Pig. Matches with the Rabbit, the Dragon, the Monkey, and the Dog will be distinctly average, while they’re better off being just friends with the Snake. When it comes to love, they should avoid the Rat, the Ox, the Rooster, and other Horses at all costs.
**_Job Prospects_**
With their excellent communication skills and desire to work as part of a team, people born in the Year of the Horse are well-suited to careers in publication, performance, journalism, sales, translation, hospitality, management, and tourism.
**_How to Manage Your Relationship with the Horse_**
Those born under the sign of the Horse are well-known for their amicable and easy-going disposition, meaning they are extremely comfortable in social situations and are able to instantly put people at ease. Their quick wit and great sense of humour mean they are popular at large social gatherings and often have a wide circle of friends. In short, forging a friendship with the Horse couldn’t be easier!
**_The Elemental Cycle_**
As we mentioned in our introductory article, the 12-year animal cycle is part of a much wider 60-year elemental cycle, meaning that each year of the zodiac is also assigned an element. People born in 1954 or 2014 belong to the Year of the Wood Horse, meaning they are predisposed to be irritable and moody, but make up for it with their active imagination and unparalleled insight. The Fire Horses, who were born in 1966 or 2026, are known for being especially lively, smart, charismatic, and enthusiastic, although their stubbornness can be off-putting.

Anyone born in 1978 is an Earth Horse, meaning that, in spite of their short-tempered nature, they are optimistic, kind-hearted, responsible, righteous, and always ready to help others. Those born in 1930 or 1990 are Metal Horses, who are kind, straightforward, calm, rational, and particularly popular among their friends. Finally, the Water Horses of 1942 and 2002 have a reliable, helpful, and amicable disposition with a capacity to skilfully charm the opposite sex, although they can be prone to sentimentality and cantankerousness.
So remember, don’t look a gift Horse in the mouth, because they’re bound to have a witty comeback!

**Peter King Nzioki Mwania** (born 25 May 1978), popularly known as **Peter King**, is a Kenyan actor.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Nzioki#cite_note-1)[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Nzioki#cite_note-pulse-2) He is best known for his roles in the films _[The Constant Gardener](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Constant\_Gardener\_(film) "The Constant Gardener (film)")_, _[The Fifth Estate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Fifth\_Estate\_(film) "The Fifth Estate (film)")_ and _[Sense8](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sense8 "Sense8")_.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Nzioki#cite_note-pulse-2)
Nzioki was born on 25 May 1978 in [Nairobi, Kenya](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nairobi "Nairobi"). His father Michael David Mwania, served in the [Kenyan Army](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya_Army "Kenya Army") and his mother worked at the military hospital. At the age of six, he joined church productions at the [Lang’ata](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lang'ata "Lang'ata") Barracks. He completed his education from Lang’ata High School in [Nairobi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nairobi "Nairobi").[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Nzioki#cite_note-kenyabuzz-3)
He is married to fellow actress Tess King.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Nzioki#cite_note-4)

He made his acting debut in 2000 at the [Kenya](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya "Kenya") National Theatre for three years under the guidance of Joab Kanuka. In theater, he played 'Iago' in the Phoenix Players production of the [Shakespeare](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Shakespeare "William Shakespeare") tragedy _[Othello](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Othello "Othello")_. In 2005, he made his film debut with a minor role in _[The Constant Gardener](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Constant\_Gardener\_(film) "The Constant Gardener (film)")_ directed by [Fernando Meirelles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fernando_Meirelles "Fernando Meirelles").[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Nzioki#cite_note-kenyabuzz-3) In the same year, he appeared as 'Barman' in the television movie _[Transit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transit\_(2005\_film) "Transit (2005 film)")_. In 2016, he appeared in the thriller film _[The CEO](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_CEO "The CEO")_ where he played the role of 'Jomo'. The film had its premier 10 July 2016, at the Eko Hotels & Suites, [Victoria Island, Lagos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Victoria_Island,_Lagos "Victoria Island, Lagos")[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Nzioki#cite_note-5) and later received critical acclaim.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Nzioki#cite_note-pulse-2)[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Nzioki#cite_note-6)[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Nzioki#cite_note-7)

After several villainous roles, he received the role as stepfather in [MTV](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MTV "MTV") series [_Shuga 2_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shuga_(TV_series) "Shuga (TV series)"), then as an inspiring soccer coach in _The Inside Story_ aired in Discovery Channel; and a preacher in _The Knife Grinder's Tale_.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Nzioki#cite_note-8)
In 2016, he was selected for the role as Kenyan crime lord '[Silas Kabaka](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sense8 "Sense8")' in the [Netflix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netflix "Netflix") series _[Sense8](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sense8 "Sense8")_.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Nzioki#cite_note-pulse-2) The role made him a popular television actor in [Kenya](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya "Kenya").

**PETER KING NZIOKI MWANIA**

Peter King Nzioki Mwania, popularly known as Peter King, born on 14 June 1979, is a Kenyan- male actor. His father was a soldier in the Kenyan Army, and his mother worked at the barracks hospital. At the age of six, he joined in church productions at the Lang’ata Barracks. He completed his Secondary School education from Lang’ata High School. He made acting debut in 2000 at the Kenya National Theatre and served for three years under the guidance of Joab Kanukaa. He is best known for his roles in the films «_The Constant Gardener_», «_The Fifth Estate_» and «_Sense8_».. In theater, he played ‘Iago’ in the «_Phoenix Players_» production of the Shakespeare tragedy «_Othello_ ». In 2005, he made his film debut with a minor role in «The Constant Gardener» directed by Fernando Meirelless. In the same year, he featured as a ‘Barman’ in the television movie «Transit». In 2016, **he featured in Kunle Afolayan’s directional Nollywood Thriller movie** «The CEO», where he played the role of ‘Jomo’ . The film had its premier 10 July 2016, at the Eko Hotels & Suites, Victoria Island, Lagos. He made out standing appearances as ‘Mkwajo’ in award-winning musical «Mo Faya» directed by Eric Wainaina. After several villainous roles, he received the role as stepfather in MTV series «Shuga 2», then as an inspiring Soccer Coach in «The Inside Story» aired on Discovery Channel; and a Preacher in «The Knife Grinder’s Tale». In 2016, he was selected for the role as Kenyan crime lord ‘Silas Kabaka’ in the television series «Sense8». This particular role made him a popular Tv actor in Kenya.
**LIZZ NJAGAH**

Elizabeth Anne Achieng’ Njagah, popularly known as Lizz Njagah was born 26 December, she is a Kenyan-Nollywood female Actress, Film Director and Producer. She has appeared in a number of television series and films. Born and bred in Nairobi, Kenya, her professional acting career began after she joined the Kenya National Theatre back in 1998. After a year’s tour of duty at the National, she was awarded the prestigious « KWAL Scholarship », a two – year intensive internship program with « Phoenix Players » where she was greatly involved in the staging of various productions. Lizz then went on tour through South Africa, Mozambique and Kenya with Seok Ho Lee’s play, Sara Bartmaan and the Four Karmas. Lizz further set out into TV and film, playing the lead character Nancy, in the TV series « Makutano Junction » which aired all across Africa on MNET and Africa Magic Channel, she played the lead character Dr. Salma in Kenya’s first medical drama « Saints ». Her big break was getting cast as fun loving series regular « Tare Duke », in Season 4, 5 and 6 of MNET [Nigeria](https://esbimedia.com/cm/michael-godson-la-star-montante-de-nollywood/)‘s Soap Opera « Tinsel » .She played the leading lady Kingo’ra in Greece/Kenya Film « Return Of Lazarus » (November, 2011). She finished production on Veve (Sept, 2014) a full length feature film from the makers of « Nairobi Half Life ». Not only a talented actress, Lizz extends and engages herself into production as well. Through her Film « Outfit ». She has produced and starred in three films. « Me, My Wife And Her Guru » (April, 2010), « Return Of Lazarus » (November, 2011), and one that hit the big screen in November 2013, a sexy comedy aptly titled « House Of Lungula », she also fetured in a web series called « In The Fores »t. She also featured in something that was a first for the Kenyan TV and Film Industry, a personality based reality show. She is not called « Kenya’s Busiest Actress » for nothing.

Lizz won a Best Actress award at the concluded London Greek Film Festival for her portrayal of a [Kenyan](https://esbimedia.com/cm/lupita-nyongo-une-femme-inspirante/) immigrant in Greek/ Kenyan road movie Return Of Lazarus.
**NICHOLAS MUTUMA**
